name: Transcribe LinkedIn video ads from the Ad Library to Google Sheets with Apify

parameters.content:
# Transcribe LinkedIn video ads from the Ad Library to Google Sheets with Apify

Take one advertiser's LinkedIn Ad Library page and get their video ads as text: headline, format, the first-3-seconds hook, full transcript, length and language, one row per ad.

### Who it's for
B2B marketers and agencies who study competitor LinkedIn campaigns and want the spoken message, not just the thumbnail.

### How it works
1. A Set node holds the advertiser's Ad Library URL and the number of ads to fetch.
2. An HTTP Request starts the LinkedIn Ad Library scraper on Apify, then an If node and a polling request wait until the run finishes.
3. The run's dataset ID is handed to the LinkedIn Ads Transcript Scraper on Apify, so no ad rows pass through n8n. Each video ad is transcribed and the hook extracted. Videos with no speech come back as uncharged misses.
4. A Code node shapes one row per ad, a Set node tidies the columns and a Google Sheets node appends them.

### Setup
1. Create an HTTP Header Auth credential (name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN`) and select it on the three HTTP Request nodes.
2. Connect Google Sheets and pick the spreadsheet and sheet.
3. Open the Config node, set the advertiser's Ad Library URL and how many ads to process.
4. Run the workflow.

### Requirements
An Apify account and a Google account.

### Customization tips
Run several advertisers by looping over a list of URLs. Keep the detail_url column to jump back to the original ad. Add a Schedule Trigger to watch an account monthly.

## 1. Configure
Your input URL and item count live in one Set node.

## 2. Scrape and wait
Start the Apify scraper run, then poll it every few seconds until it finishes.

## 3. Transcribe and shape rows
Hand the run's dataset ID to the transcript actor, then build one row per item.

## 4. Save
Append the rows to Google Sheets.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: adLibraryUrl = a LinkedIn Ad Library search URL (https://www.linkedin.com/ad-library/search?accountOwner=…&countries=…&dateOption=…) or a company URL like https://www.linkedin.com/company/hubspot/. maxAds = how many ads to pull from the Ad Library (video ads are transcribed; image ads have their on-image copy read).

nodes.name: Scrape the Ad Library (advertiser)
nodes.notes: Starts silva95gustavo/linkedin-ad-library-scraper and waits up to 60s. Returns the run object — we only need data.defaultDatasetId. To use another Ad Library scraper, swap the actor slug + the JSON body to its input fields.

nodes.name: Wait for scrape (poll run)
nodes.notes: Loops back until the scraper run finishes (each poll waits up to 60s server-side).

nodes.name: Transcribe video ads by dataset ID: hooks & transcripts
nodes.notes: Chains steadyfetch/linkedin-ads-transcript-scraper on the scraper run's dataset ID (no ad rows pass through n8n, so big batches stay light). Video ads come back transcribed (transcript + first-3s hook + advertiser metadata); image ads come back with their on-image copy read; document, carousel and text-only creatives pass through as uncharged metadata rows. Charged only when text is delivered.

nodes.name: Teardown table (one row per item)
nodes.notes: Terminal step: a clean spreadsheet-shaped row per ad. Wire Google Sheets / Airtable / Slack / a database after this node.
